tracks.title: Guzheng City
tracks.description: Welcome to "Hotel Lobbies Around the World"! Here in Guzheng City, this hotel lobby features flaming brasiers offset the triple 10 meter waterfalls.  An innovative clock made of animatronic dolphins sets the tone, while telling the time! 6 Artist alcoves on the opposite wall provide guests with entertainment while providing the artists customers! Next week, we will take a look at a very special taxidermy-themed lobby in Cudahy, Wisconsin.

tracks.title: Morning
tracks.description:
Morning. The time of day when you can’t figure out how to get to your drive-thru coffee place because there’s new construction and the sun is super low, so you’re squinting at the signs, trying to figure out if you are supposed to turn left here or if you definitely should NOT turn left here, because you will get three tires shredded by sharp, metal chunks before you fall in a hole. 

This piece of music is based on the old-timey concept of calm, beautiful, renewing mornings.

tracks.title: Evening
tracks.description: Hey Music Supervisors! Are you sick of choosing Claude Debussy's "Clair de Lune" or Ravel's "Pavane for a Dead Princess" when you're placing music for that one scene at the end of Act II where there is a sunset and an overall sense of relief? I got ya, friend!

tracks.title: Kalimba Relaxation Music
tracks.description: Can you believe kalimbas are only like $20? Check them out in my amazon affilliate store! (I do not have an amazon affiliate store.)

tracks.title: Mana Two - Part 1
tracks.description: Is nice? Is nice.

tracks.title: Mana Two - Part 2
tracks.description: You don't think mountains are timeless? What are you, a geologist? I should have recognized that by your customized beer mugs and your copper-colored Subaru.

tracks.title: Mana Two - Part 3
tracks.description: If clouds themselves hold the secret, then the secret must be moisture. Remember to hydrate!

tracks.title: Midnight Tale
tracks.description: Gather 'round the tavern's fire and I will share a tale for as long as I have ale. Hah! "Tale and ale!" I'm not guaranteeing rhymes, though. That was a coincidence. I was playing lute for an uninterested group of tavern-goers, when all of a sudden, I remembered that I had a sandwich for lunch! It looks like I'm out of ale, so that is the end of my tale.

tracks.title: Water Lily
tracks.description: Simple and elegant.

tracks.title: Dreamer
tracks.description: Gorgeous, rich piano chords run counter to subtle percussions. This piece is a workhouse for video productions. Don't bother with the preview, just download this thing. Because seriously... planning a cat rescue? This will work. Attending someone else's family reunion and trying to convince them you're related? Yes. This will work. Time lapse of a rocket assembly? Obviously. I'm looking at you, ESA!

tracks.title: Dream Culture
tracks.description: Dreamy watery piano bits over a tight percussion with some reverse effects to add to the dreamlike state of things.

tracks.title: Floating Cities
tracks.description: It is the future? It certainly sounds like it... What would I use this for? Probably a video game with non-action gameplay. Certainly a montage of some futuristic film... or maybe one of those sandwiched scenes where a person is walking in the rain, but you don't get any of the sounds of the actual rain... just this piece. No dialog, no voiceover, just walking. Do they have a name for those scenes? They must.

tracks.title: Northern Glade
tracks.description: Are you sick of "high pressure" games that "keep score"? Yeah, me too. But I FIXED it! I made a game where literally nothing happens, and nothing matters! I enjoy playing as a chicken, though it grants you no special powers. I'm not sure what chicken powers would be. Brief and ponderous flight? Speak to other chickens? Super fast egg warming? You can experience “Northern Glade” here: https://incompetech.com/games/Magic%20Scout/

tracks.title: Cottages
tracks.description: You know the old phrase "as relaxing as a toaster"? They meant any electrical machine, really. I think if a toaster were to make relaxing music this is it.

tracks.title: Manor
tracks.description: This one is a little more peppy than the others in this video experience album. Still very very blippy, though. 9.7/10 on the blippiness scale.

tracks.title: Almost New
tracks.description: Remember when you went on summer holiday to your Auntie's house outside Nether Wallop in Hampshire while your parents went to Cyprus to broker a secret deal with the Ottoman Empire?  Remember the times in the Magic Garden? This piece of music is more "Magic Garden" than "Inter-Empire Diplomacy".

tracks.title: Crinoline Dreams
tracks.instruments: Piano, Violin, Viola, Bass, Cello, Double Bass
tracks.description: You ever get the feeling to just hang out on a skating pond with a beagle?  Make sure you hit play on this track!

tracks.title: Almost Bliss
tracks.description: I love sipping lemonade by the lake when a storm approaches. I love walking through apple orchards in the fall.  I love the squeak of minivan tires being dragged onto the flatbed truck of the repo man. Memories of simpler times... so wonderful.

tracks.title: Wholesome
tracks.description: Nothing but good, wholesome instruments here. None of those dirty electric guitars, synths, drum kits, harps, sackbuts, or pipe organs. Heh, organs.

tracks.title: Valse Gymnopedie
tracks.description: This is Gymnopedie #1 from Erik Satie (1888), but it has a beat and you can dance to it.
